title: Farmland, a fire, and a witness

exchanges.a: My village is {VILLAGE}. It is about forty kilometers from {CITY}.
We had farmland, about five acres, where we grew rice and vegetables.

exchanges.q: Who tried to take your land?
a: Men who work for a local leader, {LEADER}.
They wanted the land for a factory. They offered a very low price, and my father refused.

exchanges.q: What happened after your father refused?
exchanges.a: In April 2021 they burned our house at night. My father and I got out, but my uncle was injured.

exchanges.q: Did you see who burned the house?
exchanges.a: I saw three men running toward the road. I recognized one of them; he was the driver of {LEADER}.

exchanges.q: How long did you stay in the village after the fire?
exchanges.a: Only one week. Then we went to my aunt's house in another district for six months.

exchanges.q: Why didn't you stay at your aunt's house?
exchanges.a: Because the same men came there and asked the neighbors about us. My aunt was afraid.

exchanges.q: Did you go to the police about the fire?
a: My father went the next day.
The police said that it was an accident and closed the case without investigating.

exchanges.q: What do you think would happen if you returned?
exchanges.a: I think they would hurt me, maybe kill me, because I am the one who saw the driver.
